title: LTR ratio and genome size: exploratory PGLS
legend: Nineteen species have both released genome-size estimates and primary LTR ratios (239 retained elements); 11 LTR species without genome sizes are excluded without imputation. Each hollow point is the released median of untransformed element ratios for one species. Gray bars are estimated genome-size intervals and 95% within-species element-bootstrap median intervals. Pagel-lambda PGLS fits log10(median ratio) as the response to log10(genome Gbp), by maximum likelihood with lambda constrained to [0,1], on the original branch lengths of the source tree pruned to 19 species. Each species contributes one observation; elements are not biological replicates and do not act as regression weights. The blue line is the back-transformed fitted geometric mean; its band is a 95% t-based coefficient interval, not an individual-species prediction interval. The dotted ratio-one line denotes equal terminal and internal depth. Slope 0.024196 (95% CI -0.560865 to 0.609257), P = 0.931489; lambda = 6.2e-09 at a parameter boundary. No detectable association in these 19 species; the interval permits effects in either direction. Exploratory companion, not a manuscript figure assignment. Genome sizes are D. fuscus assembly-anchored IOD-derived estimates converted at 0.978 Gbp per pg, not independent species C-values. The LTR ratio is a mapping/deletion-footprint proxy, not a deletion rate. The supplied dated tree's publication and calibration provenance remain unresolved. Coefficient intervals and P values are conditional on fitted lambda and the supplied tree; the fit does not propagate measurement uncertainty in either variable.
alt_text: Nineteen labelled species medians and gray measurement intervals on log-scaled axes, with a nearly horizontal blue PGLS fit and broad blue confidence band.
